title: Are Dense Rewards Worth Their Tokens in GRPO?
abstract: arXiv:2611.13560v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: RLVR trains language models to reason by rewarding correct final answers. A widely used algorithm, group-relative policy optimization (GRPO), gives every token of a solution the same credit, so dense process rewards have been proposed to credit intermediate steps, for example with a Monte-Carlo reward that scores each step by sampling continuations from it. Comparing such a reward with GRPO per training update, or vetting it with a gradient test on a single batch, leaves out what it costs: in our setting, the continuations alone take 91% of all generated tokens. We introduce a matched-compute protocol that gives every training intervention the same budget, measured in generated tokens and training GPU-hours, and tests it in preregistered studies with controls for side effects. Across 1,668 runs on six models, matching compute reverses the ranking. On Qwen2.5-1.5B, the Monte-Carlo reward leads standard GRPO per update, yet ends 14.3 per

translated_title: 密集奖励在GRPO中值得付出那么多token开销吗？
translated_abstract: RLVR（可验证奖励的强化学习）通过奖励正确的最终答案来训练语言模型进行推理。广泛使用的算法——组相对策略优化（GRPO）为解答中的每个token赋予相同的信用，因此有研究提出密集过程奖励来为中间步骤分配信用，例如使用蒙特卡洛奖励，通过从每个步骤采样后续内容来为该步骤评分。然而，在每个训练更新中将此类奖励与GRPO进行比较，或在单个批次上用梯度测试加以检验，都忽略了其成本：在我们的设置中，仅后续内容采样就消耗了全部生成token的91%。我们引入了一种计算匹配协议，为每种训练干预分配相同的预算（以生成的token数和训练GPU小时数衡量），并在带有副作用对照的预注册研究中进行测试。在六个模型上的1,668次运行中，计算匹配逆转了排名。在Qwen2.5-1.5B上，蒙特卡洛奖励在每个更新中领先于标准GRPO，但最终却落后14.3个百分点（摘要原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 尽管蒙特卡洛密集过程奖励在单个更新比较中优于标准GRPO，但在以生成token数和GPU小时数衡量的计算量公平匹配下，其高昂的采样开销（占生成token的91%）使结果排名发生逆转，密集奖励并不值得其token代价。
en_tdlr: Despite outperforming standard GRPO per update, dense Monte-Carlo process rewards lose under a matched-compute protocol (equal generated tokens and GPU-hours, 1,668 runs across six models), since their costly continuations—91% of all generated tokens—reverse the ranking.
